WIT02 — The philosophical/Sufi contrast: under a condition versus without a condition

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Lāhījī, Shawāriq al-ilhām, ed. Asad ʿAlīzāda, I, p.469

Page-indexed electronic transcription checked against the displayed page; print image not collated

فيكون الفرق بين هذا المذهب، ومذهب الحكماء، انهم يخصون الواجبية بمرتبة واحدة؛ هي تلك الحقيقة بشرط أن لا يتعين بشيء من الماهيات. والصوفية يجعلون الواجبية لتلك الحقيقة؛ لا بشرط أن يتعين بشيء من الماهيات.

The difference between this position and that of the philosophers would be that the philosophers restrict necessity to one rank: that reality on condition that it not become determined by any of the quiddities. The Sufis, by contrast, assign necessity to that reality without making its non-determination by any quiddity a condition.

This proposal turns on bi-sharṭ lā versus lā bi-sharṭ; those logical qualifications cannot be collapsed into a physical division of one substance. | Bounded passage, not the whole work; do not infer an exhaustive manuscript collation.

This objection is the hinge between a banal true claim about existence and the stronger unity thesis.

Lāhījī’s counter-dilemma

Lāhījī challenges the inference that existence cannot have genuine distinct instances, some self-subsistent and others dependent. Denying that a genus-like universal exists separately does not show that real existential plurality is impossible. On p.473 Lāhījī explicitly denies that proof of one self-subsisting necessary existence automatically excludes real dependent particular existences.

LAH03 — Lāhījī, p. 473: the objection to making every real existence self-subsistent

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · al-Lāhījī, Shawāriq al-ilhām, I, 473, end of Ishāra ʿirfāniyya.

New continuation: printed/digital text; manuscript collation pending

إنما يسلم في الوجود القائم بذاته، وهو الذي لا يمكن أن يكون قائما بماهية من الماهيات. ولا شبهة في كونه واجب الوجود. فمن أين يلزم أنه لا يكون وجود غير ذلك قائما بالماهيات الممكنة وأن يكون كل حقيقة وجودية قائمة بذاتها؟ وما ذكر من وجوب كون الوجود جزئيا حقيقيا، إنما هو في حقيقة وجودية قائمة بذاتها. فمن أين يلزم أن مفهوم الوجود الذي هو الكون في الأعيان ليس بكلي، وليس له أفراد حقيقية بعضها قائم بذاته وبعضها قائم بالماهيات الممكنة؟ فإن بنى على ذلك ما بنى عليه مذهب المتكلمين، من وجوه الإشكالات المذكورة، فوجوه الدفع أيضا قد عرفت مع أن الكلام في هذا البيان المنقول، وأنه كيف يدل على ذلك المطلوب؟ وإنما ثبتنا في هذه المسألة بهذا التطويل الذي لم يكن عنه من محيد، لكونها أهم أصول المعرفة وأعظم مسائل التوحيد.

That is granted only for existence subsisting through itself, which cannot subsist in any quiddity; there is no doubt that such existence is necessary. But whence does it follow that there cannot be some other existence subsisting in possible quiddities, or that every reality of existence must subsist through itself? The argument that existence must be a real individual applies only to a reality of existence that subsists through itself. How, then, does it follow that the concept of existence—being in external realities—is not universal, with genuine instances, some subsisting through themselves and others in possible quiddities? If the objections the theologians advance are built upon the interpretation in question, their replies too have already been explained. But our present discussion concerns this reported argument and how it is supposed to demonstrate the conclusion claimed. We have remained so long with this question, with no way to avoid doing so, because it is among the most important principles of knowledge of God and the greatest questions of divine unity.

This is a counter-argument, not a Sufi slogan. The question is whether the uniqueness of an intrinsically necessary individual existence implies that there cannot be dependent existences. The quantifier is critical: all real existence need not be independent simply because one independent existence is necessary. Footnote 1 clarifies 'ʿalā dhālika' as referring to the Sayyid's interpretation; footnote 2 identifies the 'reported explanation' as the Sufis'. This page is the CONCLUSION of a longer dialectic, and should not be presented as an uninterrupted full Ishāra until pp. 470–472 are checked.

C31Y01 — Priority and intensity are not interchangeable

Mullā ʿAbd Allāh al-Yazdī · Yazdī, printed p.12 (= PDF page 12), paragraphs on aqdamiyya and ashaddiyya

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

وأما التشكيك بالأقدمية فهو أن يكون صدق الكلي على بعض أفراده متقدما على صدقه على بعض آخر بالذات والعلية لا بالزمان. فإن تقدم صدق الإنسان على الأب على صدقه على الابن لا يسمى تشكيكا. وأما الأشدية فقد يفسر بأكثرية ظهور آثار الكلي في بعض الأفراد. وزيفه السيد السند بأنه يستلزم كون كثير من الذاتيات كالإنسان مثلا مقولا بالشدة والضعف لاختلاف أفرادها في استتباع الآثار؛ ثم اختار تفسيرها بما استفاده من كلام بهمنيار فهو ازدياد طبيعة العام فيها في بعض الأفراد دون بعض كالطويل بالقياس إلى الذراع والذراعين، والأسود بالقياس إلى الفحم والقير.

Gradation by precedence means that the universal's being true of some of its instances precedes its being true of others essentially and causally, rather than temporally. The prior application of “human” to the father rather than the son is not called gradation. Intensity has sometimes been explained as the more abundant manifestation of the universal's effects in certain instances. Al-Sayyid al-Sanad rejected this because it would entail that many essential predicates, such as “human,” are said with intensity and weakness, since their instances differ in the effects that follow from them. He instead chose an explanation drawn from Bahmanyār: an increase of the common nature in some instances rather than others, as with “long” in relation to one cubit and two cubits, and “black” in relation to charcoal and pitch.

Printed footnote 6 identifies al-Sayyid al-Sanad as Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Dashtakī; footnote 8 separately identifies al-Muḥaqqiq al-Sharīf as Jurjānī. Reported position, not an independently collated Dashtakī text. | The p.12 text continues after the endpoint selected here.

ثم أقول: قد اختار السيد السند ـ قدس سره ـ أن المحكي عنه هو اتحاد الموضوع مع مفهوم المحمول في الخارج. فنقول: إن كانت تلك الحكاية صادقة لزم وجود الاتحاد في الخارج، وأنه يستلزم إليه؛ وإن كانت كاذبة لم يعتبر. فإن اختار أن الاتحاد في الخارج لا أنه موجود في الخارج، فقد صار إلى ما ذكرناه سواء بسواء.

Then I say: al-Sayyid al-Sanad chose the view that what is represented is the subject's union with the concept of the predicate in the external order. We therefore say: if that representation is true, the existence of the union in the external order follows, and it entails [a regress: the printed text reads “to it”]; if it is false, it is disregarded. If he chooses to say that the union is in the external order, without saying that it exists in the external order, he has arrived at precisely what we stated.

C31L01 — A charitable interpretation in terms of manifestations

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Shawāriq I, scan printed p.462; PDF page 463; electronic p.468

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

اعلم: أن ما نقلنا من بعضهم سابقا في توجيه كلام الصوفية في وحدة الوجود مما يناسب مذهب الحكماء على ما حققنا من تحقق الحقائق المختلفة للوجود، فإنه إذا كان للوجود حقائق مختلفة متحققة ويمكن أن يتفطن بكون تلك الحقائق غير مختلفة بتمام الحقيقة، بل بالشدة والضعف، فيكون الوجود حقيقة واحدة متفاوتة في المظاهر التي هي الماهيات بحسب الشدة والضعف، والكمال والنقص. ولما كانت الوجودات المتفاوتة قائمة بالماهيات متعينة بتعيناتها، لم يلزم أن يكون اختلافها في نفس حقيقة الوجود، ليلزم التشكيك في الذاتي، بل في تعيناتها التابعة للماهيات المختلفة. وهذا في الحقيقة اختلاف في ظهور آثار الوجود قلة وكثرة، بل لما كان اختلاف الوجودات كما عرفت تبعا لاختلاف الماهيات، فمع قطع النظر عن الماهيات؛ لا اختلاف في حقيقة الوجود من حيث هي أصلا.

Know that the explanation of the Sufis' doctrine of the unity of existence which we previously transmitted from one of them accords with the philosophers' position, given what we established about distinct realities of existence. If existence has distinct realized realities, one may recognize that they differ not in their entire reality but in intensity and weakness. Existence would then be a single reality varying in its manifestations, namely the quiddities, according to intensity and weakness, perfection and deficiency. Since the varying existences subsist in quiddities and are determined by their determinations, their difference need not concern the very reality of existence, which would entail gradation in an essential constituent. It concerns instead their determinations, which follow the different quiddities. This is in reality a difference in the manifestation of existence's effects, in fewer or greater numbers. Indeed, since the difference between existences follows the difference between quiddities, as you have learned, setting the quiddities aside leaves no difference at all in the reality of existence considered as such.

Complete opening argument, spanning the end of printed 462 and first line of 463. Replaces reliance on the short WIT01 extract without deleting it.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Shawāriq I, printed p.463; PDF page 464; electronic pp.469–470

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

فيكون الفرق بين هذا المذهب، ومذهب الحكماء: أنهم يخصون الواجبية بمرتبة واحدة؛ هي تلك الحقيقة بشرط أن لا يتعين بشيء من الماهيات. والصوفية يجعلون الواجبية لتلك الحقيقة؛ لا بشرط أن يتعين بشيء من الماهيات، فيكون كل حقيقة وجودية واجبة، إذا اعتبرت من حيث هي هي، مقطوعة النظر عن التعين، وممكنة باعتبار أخذها بشرط التعين، فيكون الممكنات في الحقيقة هي التعينات، والواجب هو الحقيقة المطلقة، فلا يلزم تعدد وتكثر فيما هو واجب، ولا كون شيء من الممكنات فردا للواجب، ولا حاجة إلى أن يقال: إن تلك الحقيقة غير متعينة في حد ذاتها؛ كالكلي الطبيعي، أو أنها متعينة بتعين؛ لا ينافي شيئا من التعينات، كما ارتكبوه ليرد عليه ما أشرنا إليه سابقا، بل هي متعينة بنفس ذاتها. وهذا التعين ينافي جميع التعينات، حيث يمتنع أن يؤثر فيها شيء من التعينات، ويقارنها مقارنة تأثير؛ كمقارنة العوارض المشخصة للماهيات، وإنما المقارنة التي للتعينات معها هي مقارنة تأثر وانفعال؛ منها كمقارنة المعلول للعلة.

The difference between this position and that of the philosophers would therefore be that the philosophers restrict necessity to one rank: that reality on condition that it is not determined by any quiddity. The Sufis ascribe necessity to that reality without stipulating its determination by any quiddity. Every existential reality, considered just as it is and apart from determination, would thus be necessary, while it would be contingent when taken under the condition of determination. The contingent things would in reality be the determinations, and the Necessary would be the unrestricted reality. Neither plurality in what is necessary nor any contingent thing's being an instance of the Necessary follows. There is no need to say that this reality is intrinsically undetermined, like the natural universal, or that it has a determination compatible with all determinations, as its interpreters proposed, thereby inviting our earlier objection. Rather, it is determined through its very essence. This determination excludes all [such other] determinations in the sense that none can affect it or accompany it as an affecting factor, as individuating accidents accompany quiddities. The determinations accompany it instead as things affected by it and receptive to it, as an effect accompanies its cause.

The restrictive clause explains ينافي: causal invulnerability, not an unqualified denial of any relation to determinations. | lā bi-sharṭ is being taken without a condition; bi-sharṭ lā imposes a negative condition.

C31L03 — The interpretation tracks a claim about spreading and manifestation

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Shawāriq I, printed pp.463–464; PDF pages 464–465; electronic p.470

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

ولا إلى أن يقال: إن ذلك طور وراء طور العقل؛ إلا أن يراد العقول العامية الرسمية، فيكون أكثر المسائل العقلية كذلك. وهذا التوجيه إنما هو على مطابقة ظاهر قولهم؛ من أن الوجود مع كونه عين الواجب، وغير قابل للتجزي والانقسام، قد انبسط على هياكل الموجودات، وظهر فيها، فلا يخلو عنه شيء من الأشياء، بل هو حقيقتها وعينها، وإنما امتازت وتعددت بتقيدات وتعينات اعتبارية. وتمثل لذلك أمثلة لا حاجة إلى ذكرها.

Nor is there any need to say that this is a stage beyond the stage of intellect—unless ordinary, conventional intellects are meant, in which case most intellectual questions would be like that. This interpretation accords with the apparent sense of their statement that existence, although identical with the Necessary and incapable of partition or division, has spread over the structures of existent things and appeared in them. Nothing is devoid of it; rather, it is their reality and their very identity. They are distinguished and multiplied only by mentally considered restrictions and determinations. Examples are given for this which need not be mentioned.

Completes the first proposed interpretation before وقد يوجه introduces another. “Mentally considered” renders iʿtibārī without prematurely deciding all its ontological implications.

C31L04 — The alternative argument: whatever differs from existence is dependent

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī reporting an alternative interpretation · Shawāriq I, printed p.464 to opening of 465; PDF pages 465–466; electronic p.471

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

وقد يوجه بحيث لا يلزم القول بالانبساط، ومخالطته مع التعينات، لعدم إمكان عروض الوجود الذي هو الواجب القائم بذاته لشيء من الماهيات. والدليل على كون الوجود هو الواجب: أن كل مفهوم مغاير لحقيقة الوجود كالإنسان مثلا، فإنه ما لم ينضم إليه الوجود بوجه من الوجوه في نفس الأمر لم يكن موجودا فيها قطعا، وما لم يلاحظ العقل انضمام الوجود إليه لم يمكن له الحكم بكونه موجودا. فكل مفهوم مغاير للوجود، فهو في كونه موجودا في نفس الأمر محتاج إلى غيره الذي هو الوجود، وكل ما هو محتاج في كونه موجودا إلى غيره فهو ممكن، إذ لا معنى للممكن إلا ما يحتاج في كونه موجودا إلى غيره، سواء كان ذلك الغير موجدا له أو وجودا له، وكل مفهوم مغاير للوجود ممكن، ولا شيء من الممكن بواجب، فلا شيء من المفهومات المغايرة للوجود بواجب. وقد ثبت بالبرهان أن الواجب موجود، فهو لا يكون إلا الوجود الذي هو موجود بذاته، ويستغني في كونه موجودا عن غير ذاته، وإن كان المتبادر من لفظ الموجود بحسب اللغة ما قام به الوجود، فإن المتبع هو ما أدى إليه البرهان لا غير.

It may also be interpreted without entailing that existence spreads or mingles with determinations, since the existence which is the self-subsisting Necessary cannot be an accident of any quiddity. The argument that existence is the Necessary is this. Any concept different from the reality of existence, such as “human,” certainly does not exist in objective actuality unless existence is joined to it in some manner. Unless the intellect considers existence joined to it, it cannot judge it to exist. Every concept different from existence therefore depends, for its existence in objective actuality, on something other than itself, namely existence. Whatever depends on another for being existent is contingent: a contingent is precisely what needs another in order to exist, whether that other produces it or is its existence. Every concept different from existence is contingent; nothing contingent is necessary; hence no concept different from existence is necessary. It has been demonstrated that the Necessary exists. It must therefore be existence, which exists through itself and needs nothing other than its essence in order to exist. Even if the linguistic sense first suggested by “existent” is something in which existence subsists, what must be followed is the result of demonstration alone.

This is the argument under report, not Lāhījī’s final endorsement. Nafs al-amr means objective actuality here.

C31L05 — Existence as a real particular; existent as a universal predicate

Lāhījī reporting al-Muḥaqqiq al-Sharīf and Dawwānī · Shawāriq I, printed p.465; PDF page 466; electronic p.472

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

ولما وجب كون الواجب جزئيا حقيقيا متعينا بنفس ذاته، فإنما بذاته وجب أن يكون الوجود أيضا لكونه هو الواجب كذلك، فلا يكون الوجود مفهوما كليا ليمكن له أفراد، فهو جزئي حقيقي ليس فيه إمكان تعدد ولا انقسام، وقائم بذاته منزه عن كونه عارضا لغيره، فيكون الواجب هو الوجود المطلق؛ أي المعرى عن التقيد بغيره والانضمام إليه. وعلى هذا لا يتصور عروض الوجود للماهيات الممكنة، فليس معنى كونها موجودة إلا أن لها نسبة مخصوصة إلى حضرة الوجود القائم بذاته، وتلك النسبة على وجوه مختلفة وأنحاء شتى يتعذر الاطلاع على ماهياتها، فالموجود كلي وإن كان الوجود جزئيا حقيقيا. كذا ذكره المحقق الشريف ملخصا لما ذكره بعض محققي مشايخهم، وأنه قال: ولا يعلمه إلا الراسخون في العلم، وتبعه المحقق الدواني في اختيار هذا التوجيه، ونسبه إلى ذوق المتألهين. وهو إنما يناسب مذهب المتكلمين النافين لكون الوجود ذا أفراد حقيقية كما لا يخفى.

Since the Necessary must be a real particular determined through its own essence, existence too, because it is the Necessary, must be so. Existence would not be a universal concept capable of having instances, but a real particular incapable of multiplicity or division, subsisting through itself and exempt from being an accident of another. The Necessary would thus be unrestricted existence: existence stripped of restriction by, or conjunction with, anything else. On this account existence cannot be an accident of contingent quiddities. Their being existent means only that they have a specific relation to the presence of self-subsisting existence. This relation takes different forms and diverse modes whose quiddities cannot be apprehended. Thus “existent” is universal although “existence” is a real particular. Al-Muḥaqqiq al-Sharīf stated this as a summary of what one of their accomplished masters had said, adding that only those firmly rooted in knowledge know it. Al-Muḥaqqiq al-Dawwānī followed him in choosing this interpretation and attributed it to the “taste of the theosophers” [dhawq al-mutaʾallihīn]. This, however, accords only with the theologians' position denying that existence has real instances, as is evident.

Here al-Muḥaqqiq al-Sharīf is the reported source conventionally identified as Jurjānī; do not confuse with the distinct title al-Sayyid al-Sanad in Yazdī. | A mediated account of Dawwānī’s adoption; not a transcript of any of the five original glosses.

ولعمري أن هذا التوجيه لا يسمن ولا يغني من جوع، فإن كون الوجود موجودا بذاته ومستغنيا في كونه موجودا عن غير ذاته، إنما يسلم في الوجود القائم بذاته، وهو الذي لا يمكن أن يكون قائما بماهية من الماهيات، ولا شبهة في كونه واجب الوجود، فمن أين يلزم أنه لا يكون وجود غير ذلك قائما بالماهيات الممكنة وأن يكون كل حقيقة وجودية قائمة بذاتها؟ وما ذكر من وجوب كون الوجود جزئيا حقيقيا إنما هو في حقيقة وجودية قائمة بذاتها، فمن أين يلزم أن مفهوم الوجود الذي هو الكون في الأعيان ليس بكلي، وليس له أفراد حقيقية بعضها قائم بذاته وبعضها قائم بالماهيات الممكنة؟ فإن بني على ذلك ما بني عليه مذهب المتكلمين، من وجوه الإشكالات المذكورة، فوجوه الدفع أيضا قد عرفت، مع أن الكلام في هذا البيان المنقول، وأنه كيف دل على ذلك المطلوب؟ وإنما بسطنا في هذه المسألة بهذا التطويل الذي لم يكن عنه من محيد، لكونها أهم أصول المعرفة وأعظم مسائل التوحيد.

By my life, this interpretation neither nourishes nor relieves hunger. That existence exists through itself and needs nothing other than its essence in order to exist is conceded only of self-subsisting existence, which cannot subsist in a quiddity. There is no doubt that this is necessarily existent. But how does it follow that there cannot be an existence other than it, subsisting in contingent quiddities, or that every existential reality must subsist through itself? The requirement that existence be a real particular concerns only a self-subsisting existential reality. How does it follow that the concept of existence, namely being in concrete reality, is not universal and does not have real instances, some self-subsisting and others subsisting in contingent quiddities? If this conclusion is based on the objections supporting the theologians' position, you have already learned their answers. Moreover, our present question concerns this transmitted argument: how does it establish that conclusion? We have treated this question at such unavoidable length because it is among the most important foundations of knowledge and the greatest questions concerning divine unity.

Completes the Ishāra ʿirfāniyya main text; printed p.467 opens a new numbered question. Does not establish the completeness of the whole Shawāriq.

Q28 The hierarchy of lights, presence and imaginal forms

How do Illuminationist lights, intellects, suspended forms, and existential determinations relate—and where do their accounts diverge?

An ontology of light can describe the First as self-manifest, the order of lesser lights as dependent and knowledge as a relation of presence or disclosure. Yet *imaginal form*, *mental form*, *soul*, *light*, and *separated intellect* are different notions. Treating every mention of form or light as equivalent to waḥdat al-wujūd obscures the questions about representational cognition and the ontology of the imaginal.

Dawwānī’s hierarchy of lights

Dawwānī interprets al-Qayyūm as the one subsisting by Himself on whom other beings depend, and describes lights as terminating in their origin. This connects ontological dependence to the imagery and theory of light.

E1 — Dawwānī: the Self-Subsisting as the origin of the hierarchy of lights

al-Dawwānī · Jalāl al-Dīn al-Dawwānī · commentary on Suhrawardī’s Hayākil al-nūr, in Thalāth rasāʾil, p. 180 (selected lemma and explanation)

Inherited extract: direct source/voice/collation still needs full audit

[والقيّوم] الموجود بذاته الموجد لغيره لأنّه ممكن فلا بدّ له من مقوّم وينتهى إلى ما لا يكون تقوّمه بغيره لبطلان الدّور والتسلسل. [والقيّوم هو ظاهر بذاته] لأنّه هو النّور الّذي ينتهى جميع الأنوار في سلسلة الاحتياج إليه بل جميع الأنوار شعل من نوره.

[Lemma: “The Self-Subsisting” (al-Qayyūm).] He exists through Himself and brings other things into being. Since another thing is possible in itself, it requires something upon which it depends for its standing [مقوّم]; the regress must terminate in that whose standing does not come from another, since a circle and an infinite regress are impossible. [Lemma: “The Self-Subsisting is manifest through Himself.”] For He is the Light at which all lights terminate in their chain of dependence [سلسلة الاحتياج]; indeed, all lights are sparks of His light.

READING NOTE Square-bracketed statements are Suhrawardī’s lemmas in the printed commentary, not new claims authored by Dawwānī. The surrounding explanations belong to Dawwānī. The use of a light hierarchy should be compared carefully with the Qūnawī–Fanārī objection that a hierarchy of intermediaries is not the whole causal account. | Arabic source: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/8221/180?lang=fa

The phrase “sparks of His light” requires commentary; it does not by itself assert numerical identity.

The alternative imaginal ontology

Ghiyāth al-Dīn al-Dashtakī reports a doctrine of suspended imaginal exemplars that do not inhere in bodily subjects, distinguishing them from ordinary images in an individual brain.

E2 — Dashtakī: the suspended images and the ancient theosophers

Ghiyāth al-Dīn al-Dashtakī · Ghiyāth al-Dīn Manṣūr al-Dashtakī · Ishrāq Hayākil al-nūr, ed. Awjabī, printed p. 252 (short continuous passage)

Inherited extract: direct source/voice/collation still needs full audit

وأمّا الحكماء، فلأنّ أفلاطون وبقراط وفيثاغورس وأنباذقلس وغيرهم من الأقدمين المتألّهين كانوا يقولون بالمثل الخيالية المعلّقة لا في محلّ، المستنيرة والمظلمة؛ ويذهبون إلى أنّها جواهر مجرّدة مفارقة للموادّ ثابتة في الفكر والتخيّل والنفس.

As for the philosophers: Plato, Hippocrates, Pythagoras, Empedocles, and other ancient divinely oriented sages affirmed imaginal exemplars [المثل الخيالية] suspended without inhering in a substrate, some luminous and some dark. They held these to be immaterial substances, separated from matter and established in thought, imagination, and the soul.

READING NOTE This passage provides a direct text of Dashtakī on the ontology of imaginal forms, but it is NOT an immediate rebuttal of the Dawwānī passage E1. The philosophical questions to pursue are whether imaginal forms are ontologically independent of sensible bodies and whether such a realm can be assimilated to either Avicennian mental forms or the Akbarī world of images. | Arabic source: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/8256/348?lang=ar

This report is about the reality of imaginal forms, not proof of illuminationist unity.

Knowledge by presence

Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī considers the absence of a veil and the pure manifestation of the Light of Lights as conditions in illuminative knowledge. This is a dispute over how an immaterial knower knows, not an argument about corporeal motion.

QTS15 — Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī: knowledge by illumination and the absence of a veil

Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī · Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī, Sharḥ Ḥikmat al-ishrāq, printed p. 346, ch. 10.

New continuation: printed/digital text; manuscript collation pending

إذا كان عدم الحجاب كافيا في العلم الإشراقي الحضوري، ونور الأنوار نور محض، لا يمكن احتجابه عن ذاته ولا احتجاب غيره من الموجودات العقلية والحسية عنه. فنور الأنوار ظاهر لذاته، أي مدرك لها، على ما سبق بيانه في كل مجرد، وغيره ظاهر له، فيكون مدركا له، «لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض» إذ لا يحجبه شيء عن شيء. وإذ لم يحجبه شيء عن شيء، فيدرك جميع الأشياء بالإشراق الحضوري، الذي هو أشرف أنحاء الإدراك، لا بصور في ذاته، فيتكثر ذاته المقدسة وجهاته، لكونه فاعلا وقابلا، مع أن جهة الفعل غير جهة القبول، فلا يكون واحدا حقيقيا.

If the absence of a veil suffices for illuminative, presentational knowledge, and the Light of Lights is pure light, it cannot be veiled from itself, nor can other intelligible and sensible existents be veiled from it. Thus the Light of Lights is manifest to itself—that is, knows itself, as explained previously for every immaterial being—and other things are manifest to it, and therefore known by it: 'Not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or the earth escapes Him,' since nothing conceals one thing from Him by another. Since nothing conceals any thing from Him, He knows all things through knowledge by presence and illumination, the noblest mode of cognition, not through forms inhering in His essence. Were such forms to inhere in Him, His sacred essence and aspects would be multiplied, because He would be both agent and recipient, although the aspect of acting differs from that of receiving; He would no longer be genuinely one.

This is a *parallel Illuminationist primary source* from a commentary on Suhrawardī's Ḥikmat al-ishrāq, not a Tajrīd ḥāshiya. The chapter opening on this same page discusses visual perception and the elimination of the opacity/barrier model; this bounded argument is the theological application. Printed text on web is a mixed commentary context: a close critical edition must compare the base lemma with the Shīrāzī gloss before assigning each sentence exclusively to Shīrāzī.

The full *Ḥikmat al-Ishrāq* context and the alternate explanations of vision remain needed.

C31L01 — A charitable interpretation in terms of manifestations

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Shawāriq I, scan printed p.462; PDF page 463; electronic p.468

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

اعلم: أن ما نقلنا من بعضهم سابقا في توجيه كلام الصوفية في وحدة الوجود مما يناسب مذهب الحكماء على ما حققنا من تحقق الحقائق المختلفة للوجود، فإنه إذا كان للوجود حقائق مختلفة متحققة ويمكن أن يتفطن بكون تلك الحقائق غير مختلفة بتمام الحقيقة، بل بالشدة والضعف، فيكون الوجود حقيقة واحدة متفاوتة في المظاهر التي هي الماهيات بحسب الشدة والضعف، والكمال والنقص. ولما كانت الوجودات المتفاوتة قائمة بالماهيات متعينة بتعيناتها، لم يلزم أن يكون اختلافها في نفس حقيقة الوجود، ليلزم التشكيك في الذاتي، بل في تعيناتها التابعة للماهيات المختلفة. وهذا في الحقيقة اختلاف في ظهور آثار الوجود قلة وكثرة، بل لما كان اختلاف الوجودات كما عرفت تبعا لاختلاف الماهيات، فمع قطع النظر عن الماهيات؛ لا اختلاف في حقيقة الوجود من حيث هي أصلا.

Know that the explanation of the Sufis' doctrine of the unity of existence which we previously transmitted from one of them accords with the philosophers' position, given what we established about distinct realities of existence. If existence has distinct realized realities, one may recognize that they differ not in their entire reality but in intensity and weakness. Existence would then be a single reality varying in its manifestations, namely the quiddities, according to intensity and weakness, perfection and deficiency. Since the varying existences subsist in quiddities and are determined by their determinations, their difference need not concern the very reality of existence, which would entail gradation in an essential constituent. It concerns instead their determinations, which follow the different quiddities. This is in reality a difference in the manifestation of existence's effects, in fewer or greater numbers. Indeed, since the difference between existences follows the difference between quiddities, as you have learned, setting the quiddities aside leaves no difference at all in the reality of existence considered as such.

Complete opening argument, spanning the end of printed 462 and first line of 463. Replaces reliance on the short WIT01 extract without deleting it.

C31L02 — Necessity with and without a condition

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Shawāriq I, printed p.463; PDF page 464; electronic pp.469–470

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

فيكون الفرق بين هذا المذهب، ومذهب الحكماء: أنهم يخصون الواجبية بمرتبة واحدة؛ هي تلك الحقيقة بشرط أن لا يتعين بشيء من الماهيات. والصوفية يجعلون الواجبية لتلك الحقيقة؛ لا بشرط أن يتعين بشيء من الماهيات، فيكون كل حقيقة وجودية واجبة، إذا اعتبرت من حيث هي هي، مقطوعة النظر عن التعين، وممكنة باعتبار أخذها بشرط التعين، فيكون الممكنات في الحقيقة هي التعينات، والواجب هو الحقيقة المطلقة، فلا يلزم تعدد وتكثر فيما هو واجب، ولا كون شيء من الممكنات فردا للواجب، ولا حاجة إلى أن يقال: إن تلك الحقيقة غير متعينة في حد ذاتها؛ كالكلي الطبيعي، أو أنها متعينة بتعين؛ لا ينافي شيئا من التعينات، كما ارتكبوه ليرد عليه ما أشرنا إليه سابقا، بل هي متعينة بنفس ذاتها. وهذا التعين ينافي جميع التعينات، حيث يمتنع أن يؤثر فيها شيء من التعينات، ويقارنها مقارنة تأثير؛ كمقارنة العوارض المشخصة للماهيات، وإنما المقارنة التي للتعينات معها هي مقارنة تأثر وانفعال؛ منها كمقارنة المعلول للعلة.

The difference between this position and that of the philosophers would therefore be that the philosophers restrict necessity to one rank: that reality on condition that it is not determined by any quiddity. The Sufis ascribe necessity to that reality without stipulating its determination by any quiddity. Every existential reality, considered just as it is and apart from determination, would thus be necessary, while it would be contingent when taken under the condition of determination. The contingent things would in reality be the determinations, and the Necessary would be the unrestricted reality. Neither plurality in what is necessary nor any contingent thing's being an instance of the Necessary follows. There is no need to say that this reality is intrinsically undetermined, like the natural universal, or that it has a determination compatible with all determinations, as its interpreters proposed, thereby inviting our earlier objection. Rather, it is determined through its very essence. This determination excludes all [such other] determinations in the sense that none can affect it or accompany it as an affecting factor, as individuating accidents accompany quiddities. The determinations accompany it instead as things affected by it and receptive to it, as an effect accompanies its cause.

The restrictive clause explains ينافي: causal invulnerability, not an unqualified denial of any relation to determinations. | lā bi-sharṭ is being taken without a condition; bi-sharṭ lā imposes a negative condition.

C31L03 — The interpretation tracks a claim about spreading and manifestation

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Shawāriq I, printed pp.463–464; PDF pages 464–465; electronic p.470

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

ولا إلى أن يقال: إن ذلك طور وراء طور العقل؛ إلا أن يراد العقول العامية الرسمية، فيكون أكثر المسائل العقلية كذلك. وهذا التوجيه إنما هو على مطابقة ظاهر قولهم؛ من أن الوجود مع كونه عين الواجب، وغير قابل للتجزي والانقسام، قد انبسط على هياكل الموجودات، وظهر فيها، فلا يخلو عنه شيء من الأشياء، بل هو حقيقتها وعينها، وإنما امتازت وتعددت بتقيدات وتعينات اعتبارية. وتمثل لذلك أمثلة لا حاجة إلى ذكرها.

Nor is there any need to say that this is a stage beyond the stage of intellect—unless ordinary, conventional intellects are meant, in which case most intellectual questions would be like that. This interpretation accords with the apparent sense of their statement that existence, although identical with the Necessary and incapable of partition or division, has spread over the structures of existent things and appeared in them. Nothing is devoid of it; rather, it is their reality and their very identity. They are distinguished and multiplied only by mentally considered restrictions and determinations. Examples are given for this which need not be mentioned.

Completes the first proposed interpretation before وقد يوجه introduces another. “Mentally considered” renders iʿtibārī without prematurely deciding all its ontological implications.

C31L05 — Existence as a real particular; existent as a universal predicate

Lāhījī reporting al-Muḥaqqiq al-Sharīf and Dawwānī · Shawāriq I, printed p.465; PDF page 466; electronic p.472

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

ولما وجب كون الواجب جزئيا حقيقيا متعينا بنفس ذاته، فإنما بذاته وجب أن يكون الوجود أيضا لكونه هو الواجب كذلك، فلا يكون الوجود مفهوما كليا ليمكن له أفراد، فهو جزئي حقيقي ليس فيه إمكان تعدد ولا انقسام، وقائم بذاته منزه عن كونه عارضا لغيره، فيكون الواجب هو الوجود المطلق؛ أي المعرى عن التقيد بغيره والانضمام إليه. وعلى هذا لا يتصور عروض الوجود للماهيات الممكنة، فليس معنى كونها موجودة إلا أن لها نسبة مخصوصة إلى حضرة الوجود القائم بذاته، وتلك النسبة على وجوه مختلفة وأنحاء شتى يتعذر الاطلاع على ماهياتها، فالموجود كلي وإن كان الوجود جزئيا حقيقيا. كذا ذكره المحقق الشريف ملخصا لما ذكره بعض محققي مشايخهم، وأنه قال: ولا يعلمه إلا الراسخون في العلم، وتبعه المحقق الدواني في اختيار هذا التوجيه، ونسبه إلى ذوق المتألهين. وهو إنما يناسب مذهب المتكلمين النافين لكون الوجود ذا أفراد حقيقية كما لا يخفى.

Since the Necessary must be a real particular determined through its own essence, existence too, because it is the Necessary, must be so. Existence would not be a universal concept capable of having instances, but a real particular incapable of multiplicity or division, subsisting through itself and exempt from being an accident of another. The Necessary would thus be unrestricted existence: existence stripped of restriction by, or conjunction with, anything else. On this account existence cannot be an accident of contingent quiddities. Their being existent means only that they have a specific relation to the presence of self-subsisting existence. This relation takes different forms and diverse modes whose quiddities cannot be apprehended. Thus “existent” is universal although “existence” is a real particular. Al-Muḥaqqiq al-Sharīf stated this as a summary of what one of their accomplished masters had said, adding that only those firmly rooted in knowledge know it. Al-Muḥaqqiq al-Dawwānī followed him in choosing this interpretation and attributed it to the “taste of the theosophers” [dhawq al-mutaʾallihīn]. This, however, accords only with the theologians' position denying that existence has real instances, as is evident.

Here al-Muḥaqqiq al-Sharīf is the reported source conventionally identified as Jurjānī; do not confuse with the distinct title al-Sayyid al-Sanad in Yazdī. | A mediated account of Dawwānī’s adoption; not a transcript of any of the five original glosses.

C31L06 — Lāhījī’s complete objection and closing judgment

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Shawāriq I, printed p.466; PDF page 467; electronic p.472 end–473

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

ولعمري أن هذا التوجيه لا يسمن ولا يغني من جوع، فإن كون الوجود موجودا بذاته ومستغنيا في كونه موجودا عن غير ذاته، إنما يسلم في الوجود القائم بذاته، وهو الذي لا يمكن أن يكون قائما بماهية من الماهيات، ولا شبهة في كونه واجب الوجود، فمن أين يلزم أنه لا يكون وجود غير ذلك قائما بالماهيات الممكنة وأن يكون كل حقيقة وجودية قائمة بذاتها؟ وما ذكر من وجوب كون الوجود جزئيا حقيقيا إنما هو في حقيقة وجودية قائمة بذاتها، فمن أين يلزم أن مفهوم الوجود الذي هو الكون في الأعيان ليس بكلي، وليس له أفراد حقيقية بعضها قائم بذاته وبعضها قائم بالماهيات الممكنة؟ فإن بني على ذلك ما بني عليه مذهب المتكلمين، من وجوه الإشكالات المذكورة، فوجوه الدفع أيضا قد عرفت، مع أن الكلام في هذا البيان المنقول، وأنه كيف دل على ذلك المطلوب؟ وإنما بسطنا في هذه المسألة بهذا التطويل الذي لم يكن عنه من محيد، لكونها أهم أصول المعرفة وأعظم مسائل التوحيد.

By my life, this interpretation neither nourishes nor relieves hunger. That existence exists through itself and needs nothing other than its essence in order to exist is conceded only of self-subsisting existence, which cannot subsist in a quiddity. There is no doubt that this is necessarily existent. But how does it follow that there cannot be an existence other than it, subsisting in contingent quiddities, or that every existential reality must subsist through itself? The requirement that existence be a real particular concerns only a self-subsisting existential reality. How does it follow that the concept of existence, namely being in concrete reality, is not universal and does not have real instances, some self-subsisting and others subsisting in contingent quiddities? If this conclusion is based on the objections supporting the theologians' position, you have already learned their answers. Moreover, our present question concerns this transmitted argument: how does it establish that conclusion? We have treated this question at such unavoidable length because it is among the most important foundations of knowledge and the greatest questions concerning divine unity.

Completes the Ishāra ʿirfāniyya main text; printed p.467 opens a new numbered question. Does not establish the completeness of the whole Shawāriq.

Interim judgment: The common theme is the difference between representation, presence and ontological hierarchy. The current evidence shows three neighbouring but distinct claims: dependence in a light hierarchy, existence of immaterial imaginal exemplars, and presentational knowledge. They must remain differentiated and then brought into conversation.

Boundary: The quoted Dawwānī and Dashtakī fragments are not the complete historical debate and cannot establish its final resolution.

Remaining: Lāhījī’s formerly missing electronic pp.470–472 are recovered and translated within the complete Ishāra main text (scan printed pp.462–466). Still required: independent edition/manuscript variants; direct verification of Jurjānī’s reported unity argument and Dawwānī’s adoption; the full original five-stage exchange and Ghiyāth’s response.

Q29 Waḥdat al-wujūd: unity, multiplicity, and criticism

If being is one, what distinguishes created things, and how do proponents and critics answer the charges of contradiction or negating creatures?

Waḥdat al-wujūd is not a single proposition without alternatives. A report of radical ontic unity may deny independent multiplicity; a gradational theory may affirm genuinely differentiated instances of being; and an account of manifestation may affirm the Real’s singularity while attributing differing kinds of relative reality to creatures. A complete debate must assign each claim to its actual speaker.

Jurjānī presents the extreme thesis and its epistemic obstacle

Jurjānī first **reports** a Sufi position in which the apparent many are determinations of one self-subsisting essence, then explains why reason’s apparent testimony to distinct existents constitutes a powerful objection and how partisans of unveiling frame their rejoinder.

JRG01 — Jurjānī, gloss I: the challenge of radical unity and the protest of reason

al-Sayyid al-Sharīf al-Jurjānī · al-Jurjānī, Ḥāshiyat Sharḥ al-Tajrīd, gloss I; Garrett 865 fols. 16a–16b, Yahuda 5373 fols. 87b–88a; ed./transcription Nicholas Heer, Five Unedited Texts, p. 2.

Heer printed introduction and edition verified; manuscript collation pending

قيل عليه: ذهب جماعة من الصوفية إلى أن ليس في الواقع إلا ذات واحدة لا تركيب فيها أصلا، بل لها صفات متعددة هي عينها، وهي حقيقة الوجود المنزهة في حد ذاتها عن شوائب العدم وسمات نقصان الإمكان، ولها تقيدات بقيود اعتبارية بحسب ذلك تتراءى موجودات متمايزة فيتوهم من ذلك تعدد حقيقي، فلما لم يقم برهان على بطلان ذلك لم يتم ما ذكره من عدم اتحاد الماهيات ولا يتم أيضا اشتراك الوجود بل لا يثبت وجود ممكن أصلا. أقول: هذا خروج عن طور العقل، فإن بداهته شاهدة بتعدد الموجودات تعددا حقيقيا، وإنما ذوات وحقائق مختلفة بالحقيقة دون الاعتبار فقط. والذاهبون إلى تلك المقالة يدعون استنادها إلى مكاشفاتهم ومشاهداتهم، وأنه لا يمكن الوصول إليها بمباحث العقل ودلالته، بل هو معزول هناك كالحس في إدراك المعقولات. وأما المتقيدون بدرجات العقل والقائلون بأن ما يشهد له العقل فمقبول وما يشهد عليه فمردود، وأنه لا طور وراءه، فيزعمون أن تلك المكاشفات والمشاهدات على تقدير صحتها مأولة بما يوافق العقل، فهم بشهادة بداهته عندهم مستغنون عن إقامة برهان على بطلان أمثال ذلك ويعدون تجويزها مكابرة لا يلتفت إليها.

[Objection reported:] A group of Sufis maintain that in reality there is nothing but one essence, in which there is absolutely no composition. It has multiple attributes that are identical with it. It is the reality of existence, itself purified of the taints of nonexistence and the marks of the deficiency of possibility. Through its restrictions by conceptual or relational qualifications, distinct existents appear; on that account, real plurality is imagined. Since no demonstration has established the falsity of this, the commentator's assertion that quiddities are not identical remains unproved, as does the common predication of existence; indeed, no possible existent is established at all. [I say:] This lies outside the province of reason. Reason's immediate evidence testifies that existents are genuinely multiple and are essences and realities different in truth, not merely in consideration. Those who hold that view claim support from their unveilings and contemplative witnessings; they maintain it cannot be attained by rational inquiries or their indications. Reason is displaced here, just as sense is in grasping intelligibles. By contrast, those who restrict themselves to the degrees of reason, holding that what reason confirms is accepted and what it rejects is rejected, and that there is no sphere beyond it, allege that, supposing those unveilings and witnessings genuine, they must be interpreted in agreement with reason. Such persons consider reason's immediate testimony sufficient to dispense with a demonstration against doctrines of this sort and deem their admission an obstinacy unworthy of attention.

VOICE: “qīla ʿalayhi” introduces an objection ascribed to a group of Sufis; “aqūlu” is Jurjānī's response. The response describes TWO epistemic orientations; it does not flatly settle which construal of unity Jurjānī himself finally endorses. It is crucial that he identifies the alleged loss of independently existent possibles as a cost of the radical reading. In the second and third glosses he explores a more rationally constrained unity thesis and also marks the limits of dialectical proof. Arabic normalized for spacing and punctuation from Nicholas Heer's transcribed Arabic, PDF printed p. 2; final diplomatic manuscript collation outstanding.

Jāmī makes the comparative programme explicit

Jāmī describes multiplicity as disclosed in loci of manifestation and declares that his treatise compares Sufi, theologian and philosopher accounts of the Necessary and the emergence of multiplicity. This is programme and metaphysical imagery, not by itself a syllogistic proof.

C1 — Jāmī sets out the comparative task

Jāmī · ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jāmī · al-Durra al-fākhira, opening (two continuous paragraphs)

Inherited extract: direct source/voice/collation still needs full audit

الحمد لله الذي تجلّى بذاته لذاته، فتعيّن في باطن علمه مجالي ذاته وصفاته، ثم انعكست آثار تلك المجالى إلى ظاهره من الباطن، فصارت الوحدة كثرة كما تشاهد وتعاين. والصلاة على من به رجعت تلك الكثرة إلى وحدتها الأولى وعلى آله وصحبه الذين لهم في وراثة هذه الفضيلة يد طولى. أما بعد، فهذه رسالة في تحقيق مذهب الصوفية والمتكلمين والحكماء المتقدمين وتقرير قولهم في وجود الواجب لذاته، وحقائق أسمائه وصفاته، وكيفية صدور الكثرة عن وحدته، من غير نقص في كمال قدسه وعزته، وما يتبع ذلك من مباحث أخر يؤدى إليه الفكر والنظر.

Praise belongs to God, who disclosed Himself to Himself by His very Essence, such that the loci of manifestation [مجالي] of His Essence and attributes became determined in the inwardness of His knowledge. Their effects were then reflected from inward to outward, and unity became multiplicity as one sees and witnesses. Blessings upon the one through whom that multiplicity returned to its first unity, and upon his family and Companions who received an abundant share of the inheritance of this excellence. To proceed: this treatise investigates the doctrines of the Sufis [الصوفية], the theologians [المتكلمون], and the earlier philosophers [الحكماء المتقدمون], and sets out their positions concerning the existence of that which is necessary through itself [الواجب لذاته], the realities of His names and attributes, and how multiplicity proceeds from His unity without any diminution of the perfection of His holiness and majesty, together with the further investigations to which thought and reflection lead.

READING NOTE The opening already expresses an Akbarī vocabulary of manifestation. The author explicitly frames the work as a comparative philosophical investigation; he does not merely assert the priority of Sufi experience over argument. | Arabic source: almuada.4umer.com, thread 6169 (al-Durra al-fākhira, opening); cf. source register

His explicit argument for the Necessary as existence is treated in Q23.

Lāhījī moves from gradation to a stronger thesis

Lāhījī first gives a graded-existence interpretation that can be made compatible with philosophers. He then distinguishes the philosophers’ qualified claim about necessary existence from the Sufis’ unqualified account of the real existence considered apart from its determinations.

يلزم أن يكون اختلافها في نفس حقيقة الوجود، ليلزم التشكيك في الذاتي، بل في تعيناتها التابعة للماهيات المختلفة. وهذا في الحقيقة اختلاف في ظهور آثار الوجود قلة وكثرة. بل لما كان اختلاف الوجودات كما عرفت تبعا لاختلاف الماهيات، فمع قطع النظر عن الماهيات لا اختلاف في حقيقة الوجود من حيث هي أصلا. فيكون الفرق بين هذا المذهب، ومذهب الحكماء، أنهم يخصون الواجبية بمرتبة واحدة؛ هي تلك الحقيقة بشرط أن لا يتعين بشيء من الماهيات. والصوفية يجعلون الواجبية لتلك الحقيقة؛ لا بشرط أن يتعين بشيء من الماهيات. فيكون كل حقيقة وجودية واجبة، إذا اعتبرت من حيث هي هي، مقطوعة النظر عن التعين. وممكنة باعتبار أخذها بشرط التعين. فتكون الممكنات في الحقيقة هي التعينات. والواجب هو الحقيقة المطلقة، فلا يلزم تعدد وتكثر فيما هو واجب، ولا كون شيء من الممكنات فردا للواجب.

... it does not follow that their difference is within the reality of existence itself, thereby introducing gradation into what is essential; rather, the difference lies in their determinations that follow upon differing quiddities. In truth, this is a difference in the appearance of existence's effects, in greater and lesser measure. Indeed, because the differences among existences, as explained, follow upon the differences among quiddities, if we abstract from quiddities there is no difference whatsoever in the reality of existence considered in itself. The difference between this doctrine and that of the philosophers is therefore that the philosophers reserve necessity for one level: that reality on condition that it is not determined by any quiddity. The Sufis, however, ascribe necessity to that reality without the condition of its not being determined by a quiddity. Every existent reality is thus necessary when considered as it is in itself, abstracting from determination, and is possible when taken on condition of determination. Possibles are therefore in truth the determinations, while the Necessary is the absolute reality. Consequently, there is neither multiplication nor plurality in what is Necessary, nor does any possible thing become an instance of the Necessary.

Faithful to the named comparison between a philosophical 'bi-sharṭ lā' (on the condition of no determination) and a Sufi 'lā bi-sharṭ' (without the condition of no determination). These qualifying constructions are not interchangeable. A reading of this PAGE ALONE must not be presented as Lāhījī's final assent: by p. 473 he objects to an inferred monopoly of independent existence. The critical middle pages 470–472 have not yet been obtained; this remains a discontinuous edition.

This is the key step at which gradation and a stronger non-dualist thesis separate.

A witness to the nonexclusive twofold vision

The brief passage attributed to Jurjānī on seeing the Real in creation and creation in the Real shows a spiritual-epistemic way of describing unity and multiplicity. It is a parallel formulation, not a solution to the third gloss’s proof.

B1 — The knower who sees both unity and multiplicity

al-Jurjānī · al-Sayyid al-Sharīf al-Jurjānī · al-Taʿrīfāt, entry dhū al-ʿaql wa-l-ʿayn (parallel text, not a Tajrīd gloss)

Inherited extract: direct source/voice/collation still needs full audit

ذو العقل والعين: هو الذي يرى الحق في الخلق، وهذا قرب النوافل، ويرى الخلق في الحق، وهذا قرب الفرائض، ولا يحتجب بأحدهما عن الآخر، بل يرى الوجود الواحد بعينه حقًّا من وجه، وخلقًا من وجه، فلا يحتجب بالكثرة عن شهود الواحد الرائي، ولا تزاحم في شهود الكثرة الخلقية، وكذا لا تزاحم في شهود أحدية الذات المتجلية في المجالي كثرة.

The possessor of both intellect and eye [ذو العقل والعين] is one who sees the Real in creation—this is the nearness of supererogatory works—and sees creation in the Real—this is the nearness of obligatory works. Neither vision veils him from the other. Rather, he sees the one existence [الوجود الواحد] itself as Real from one aspect and as creation from another. Multiplicity does not veil him from witnessing the One who sees; nor does witnessing created multiplicity exclude witnessing the unity of the Essence as it discloses itself in many loci of manifestation [المجالي].

READING NOTE This entry in the lexicon transmitted under Jurjānī’s name establishes circulation of Akbarī technical language in his intellectual milieu. It is NOT one of the three Tajrīd glosses printed by Heer and cannot substitute for their translation or prove that every Akbarī definition represents Jurjānī’s independent assent. | Arabic source: https://usul.ai/ar/t/tacrifat/103

C31L01 — A charitable interpretation in terms of manifestations

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Shawāriq I, scan printed p.462; PDF page 463; electronic p.468

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

اعلم: أن ما نقلنا من بعضهم سابقا في توجيه كلام الصوفية في وحدة الوجود مما يناسب مذهب الحكماء على ما حققنا من تحقق الحقائق المختلفة للوجود، فإنه إذا كان للوجود حقائق مختلفة متحققة ويمكن أن يتفطن بكون تلك الحقائق غير مختلفة بتمام الحقيقة، بل بالشدة والضعف، فيكون الوجود حقيقة واحدة متفاوتة في المظاهر التي هي الماهيات بحسب الشدة والضعف، والكمال والنقص. ولما كانت الوجودات المتفاوتة قائمة بالماهيات متعينة بتعيناتها، لم يلزم أن يكون اختلافها في نفس حقيقة الوجود، ليلزم التشكيك في الذاتي، بل في تعيناتها التابعة للماهيات المختلفة. وهذا في الحقيقة اختلاف في ظهور آثار الوجود قلة وكثرة، بل لما كان اختلاف الوجودات كما عرفت تبعا لاختلاف الماهيات، فمع قطع النظر عن الماهيات؛ لا اختلاف في حقيقة الوجود من حيث هي أصلا.

Know that the explanation of the Sufis' doctrine of the unity of existence which we previously transmitted from one of them accords with the philosophers' position, given what we established about distinct realities of existence. If existence has distinct realized realities, one may recognize that they differ not in their entire reality but in intensity and weakness. Existence would then be a single reality varying in its manifestations, namely the quiddities, according to intensity and weakness, perfection and deficiency. Since the varying existences subsist in quiddities and are determined by their determinations, their difference need not concern the very reality of existence, which would entail gradation in an essential constituent. It concerns instead their determinations, which follow the different quiddities. This is in reality a difference in the manifestation of existence's effects, in fewer or greater numbers. Indeed, since the difference between existences follows the difference between quiddities, as you have learned, setting the quiddities aside leaves no difference at all in the reality of existence considered as such.

Complete opening argument, spanning the end of printed 462 and first line of 463. Replaces reliance on the short WIT01 extract without deleting it.

C31L02 — Necessity with and without a condition

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Shawāriq I, printed p.463; PDF page 464; electronic pp.469–470

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

فيكون الفرق بين هذا المذهب، ومذهب الحكماء: أنهم يخصون الواجبية بمرتبة واحدة؛ هي تلك الحقيقة بشرط أن لا يتعين بشيء من الماهيات. والصوفية يجعلون الواجبية لتلك الحقيقة؛ لا بشرط أن يتعين بشيء من الماهيات، فيكون كل حقيقة وجودية واجبة، إذا اعتبرت من حيث هي هي، مقطوعة النظر عن التعين، وممكنة باعتبار أخذها بشرط التعين، فيكون الممكنات في الحقيقة هي التعينات، والواجب هو الحقيقة المطلقة، فلا يلزم تعدد وتكثر فيما هو واجب، ولا كون شيء من الممكنات فردا للواجب، ولا حاجة إلى أن يقال: إن تلك الحقيقة غير متعينة في حد ذاتها؛ كالكلي الطبيعي، أو أنها متعينة بتعين؛ لا ينافي شيئا من التعينات، كما ارتكبوه ليرد عليه ما أشرنا إليه سابقا، بل هي متعينة بنفس ذاتها. وهذا التعين ينافي جميع التعينات، حيث يمتنع أن يؤثر فيها شيء من التعينات، ويقارنها مقارنة تأثير؛ كمقارنة العوارض المشخصة للماهيات، وإنما المقارنة التي للتعينات معها هي مقارنة تأثر وانفعال؛ منها كمقارنة المعلول للعلة.

The difference between this position and that of the philosophers would therefore be that the philosophers restrict necessity to one rank: that reality on condition that it is not determined by any quiddity. The Sufis ascribe necessity to that reality without stipulating its determination by any quiddity. Every existential reality, considered just as it is and apart from determination, would thus be necessary, while it would be contingent when taken under the condition of determination. The contingent things would in reality be the determinations, and the Necessary would be the unrestricted reality. Neither plurality in what is necessary nor any contingent thing's being an instance of the Necessary follows. There is no need to say that this reality is intrinsically undetermined, like the natural universal, or that it has a determination compatible with all determinations, as its interpreters proposed, thereby inviting our earlier objection. Rather, it is determined through its very essence. This determination excludes all [such other] determinations in the sense that none can affect it or accompany it as an affecting factor, as individuating accidents accompany quiddities. The determinations accompany it instead as things affected by it and receptive to it, as an effect accompanies its cause.

The restrictive clause explains ينافي: causal invulnerability, not an unqualified denial of any relation to determinations. | lā bi-sharṭ is being taken without a condition; bi-sharṭ lā imposes a negative condition.

C31L03 — The interpretation tracks a claim about spreading and manifestation

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Shawāriq I, printed pp.463–464; PDF pages 464–465; electronic p.470

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

ولا إلى أن يقال: إن ذلك طور وراء طور العقل؛ إلا أن يراد العقول العامية الرسمية، فيكون أكثر المسائل العقلية كذلك. وهذا التوجيه إنما هو على مطابقة ظاهر قولهم؛ من أن الوجود مع كونه عين الواجب، وغير قابل للتجزي والانقسام، قد انبسط على هياكل الموجودات، وظهر فيها، فلا يخلو عنه شيء من الأشياء، بل هو حقيقتها وعينها، وإنما امتازت وتعددت بتقيدات وتعينات اعتبارية. وتمثل لذلك أمثلة لا حاجة إلى ذكرها.

Nor is there any need to say that this is a stage beyond the stage of intellect—unless ordinary, conventional intellects are meant, in which case most intellectual questions would be like that. This interpretation accords with the apparent sense of their statement that existence, although identical with the Necessary and incapable of partition or division, has spread over the structures of existent things and appeared in them. Nothing is devoid of it; rather, it is their reality and their very identity. They are distinguished and multiplied only by mentally considered restrictions and determinations. Examples are given for this which need not be mentioned.

Completes the first proposed interpretation before وقد يوجه introduces another. “Mentally considered” renders iʿtibārī without prematurely deciding all its ontological implications.

C31L04 — The alternative argument: whatever differs from existence is dependent

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī reporting an alternative interpretation · Shawāriq I, printed p.464 to opening of 465; PDF pages 465–466; electronic p.471

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

وقد يوجه بحيث لا يلزم القول بالانبساط، ومخالطته مع التعينات، لعدم إمكان عروض الوجود الذي هو الواجب القائم بذاته لشيء من الماهيات. والدليل على كون الوجود هو الواجب: أن كل مفهوم مغاير لحقيقة الوجود كالإنسان مثلا، فإنه ما لم ينضم إليه الوجود بوجه من الوجوه في نفس الأمر لم يكن موجودا فيها قطعا، وما لم يلاحظ العقل انضمام الوجود إليه لم يمكن له الحكم بكونه موجودا. فكل مفهوم مغاير للوجود، فهو في كونه موجودا في نفس الأمر محتاج إلى غيره الذي هو الوجود، وكل ما هو محتاج في كونه موجودا إلى غيره فهو ممكن، إذ لا معنى للممكن إلا ما يحتاج في كونه موجودا إلى غيره، سواء كان ذلك الغير موجدا له أو وجودا له، وكل مفهوم مغاير للوجود ممكن، ولا شيء من الممكن بواجب، فلا شيء من المفهومات المغايرة للوجود بواجب. وقد ثبت بالبرهان أن الواجب موجود، فهو لا يكون إلا الوجود الذي هو موجود بذاته، ويستغني في كونه موجودا عن غير ذاته، وإن كان المتبادر من لفظ الموجود بحسب اللغة ما قام به الوجود، فإن المتبع هو ما أدى إليه البرهان لا غير.

It may also be interpreted without entailing that existence spreads or mingles with determinations, since the existence which is the self-subsisting Necessary cannot be an accident of any quiddity. The argument that existence is the Necessary is this. Any concept different from the reality of existence, such as “human,” certainly does not exist in objective actuality unless existence is joined to it in some manner. Unless the intellect considers existence joined to it, it cannot judge it to exist. Every concept different from existence therefore depends, for its existence in objective actuality, on something other than itself, namely existence. Whatever depends on another for being existent is contingent: a contingent is precisely what needs another in order to exist, whether that other produces it or is its existence. Every concept different from existence is contingent; nothing contingent is necessary; hence no concept different from existence is necessary. It has been demonstrated that the Necessary exists. It must therefore be existence, which exists through itself and needs nothing other than its essence in order to exist. Even if the linguistic sense first suggested by “existent” is something in which existence subsists, what must be followed is the result of demonstration alone.

This is the argument under report, not Lāhījī’s final endorsement. Nafs al-amr means objective actuality here.

C31L05 — Existence as a real particular; existent as a universal predicate

Lāhījī reporting al-Muḥaqqiq al-Sharīf and Dawwānī · Shawāriq I, printed p.465; PDF page 466; electronic p.472

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

ولما وجب كون الواجب جزئيا حقيقيا متعينا بنفس ذاته، فإنما بذاته وجب أن يكون الوجود أيضا لكونه هو الواجب كذلك، فلا يكون الوجود مفهوما كليا ليمكن له أفراد، فهو جزئي حقيقي ليس فيه إمكان تعدد ولا انقسام، وقائم بذاته منزه عن كونه عارضا لغيره، فيكون الواجب هو الوجود المطلق؛ أي المعرى عن التقيد بغيره والانضمام إليه. وعلى هذا لا يتصور عروض الوجود للماهيات الممكنة، فليس معنى كونها موجودة إلا أن لها نسبة مخصوصة إلى حضرة الوجود القائم بذاته، وتلك النسبة على وجوه مختلفة وأنحاء شتى يتعذر الاطلاع على ماهياتها، فالموجود كلي وإن كان الوجود جزئيا حقيقيا. كذا ذكره المحقق الشريف ملخصا لما ذكره بعض محققي مشايخهم، وأنه قال: ولا يعلمه إلا الراسخون في العلم، وتبعه المحقق الدواني في اختيار هذا التوجيه، ونسبه إلى ذوق المتألهين. وهو إنما يناسب مذهب المتكلمين النافين لكون الوجود ذا أفراد حقيقية كما لا يخفى.

Since the Necessary must be a real particular determined through its own essence, existence too, because it is the Necessary, must be so. Existence would not be a universal concept capable of having instances, but a real particular incapable of multiplicity or division, subsisting through itself and exempt from being an accident of another. The Necessary would thus be unrestricted existence: existence stripped of restriction by, or conjunction with, anything else. On this account existence cannot be an accident of contingent quiddities. Their being existent means only that they have a specific relation to the presence of self-subsisting existence. This relation takes different forms and diverse modes whose quiddities cannot be apprehended. Thus “existent” is universal although “existence” is a real particular. Al-Muḥaqqiq al-Sharīf stated this as a summary of what one of their accomplished masters had said, adding that only those firmly rooted in knowledge know it. Al-Muḥaqqiq al-Dawwānī followed him in choosing this interpretation and attributed it to the “taste of the theosophers” [dhawq al-mutaʾallihīn]. This, however, accords only with the theologians' position denying that existence has real instances, as is evident.

Here al-Muḥaqqiq al-Sharīf is the reported source conventionally identified as Jurjānī; do not confuse with the distinct title al-Sayyid al-Sanad in Yazdī. | A mediated account of Dawwānī’s adoption; not a transcript of any of the five original glosses.

C31L06 — Lāhījī’s complete objection and closing judgment

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Shawāriq I, printed p.466; PDF page 467; electronic p.472 end–473

Printed page image inspected; normalized Arabic transcription and fresh working translation

ولعمري أن هذا التوجيه لا يسمن ولا يغني من جوع، فإن كون الوجود موجودا بذاته ومستغنيا في كونه موجودا عن غير ذاته، إنما يسلم في الوجود القائم بذاته، وهو الذي لا يمكن أن يكون قائما بماهية من الماهيات، ولا شبهة في كونه واجب الوجود، فمن أين يلزم أنه لا يكون وجود غير ذلك قائما بالماهيات الممكنة وأن يكون كل حقيقة وجودية قائمة بذاتها؟ وما ذكر من وجوب كون الوجود جزئيا حقيقيا إنما هو في حقيقة وجودية قائمة بذاتها، فمن أين يلزم أن مفهوم الوجود الذي هو الكون في الأعيان ليس بكلي، وليس له أفراد حقيقية بعضها قائم بذاته وبعضها قائم بالماهيات الممكنة؟ فإن بني على ذلك ما بني عليه مذهب المتكلمين، من وجوه الإشكالات المذكورة، فوجوه الدفع أيضا قد عرفت، مع أن الكلام في هذا البيان المنقول، وأنه كيف دل على ذلك المطلوب؟ وإنما بسطنا في هذه المسألة بهذا التطويل الذي لم يكن عنه من محيد، لكونها أهم أصول المعرفة وأعظم مسائل التوحيد.

By my life, this interpretation neither nourishes nor relieves hunger. That existence exists through itself and needs nothing other than its essence in order to exist is conceded only of self-subsisting existence, which cannot subsist in a quiddity. There is no doubt that this is necessarily existent. But how does it follow that there cannot be an existence other than it, subsisting in contingent quiddities, or that every existential reality must subsist through itself? The requirement that existence be a real particular concerns only a self-subsisting existential reality. How does it follow that the concept of existence, namely being in concrete reality, is not universal and does not have real instances, some self-subsisting and others subsisting in contingent quiddities? If this conclusion is based on the objections supporting the theologians' position, you have already learned their answers. Moreover, our present question concerns this transmitted argument: how does it establish that conclusion? We have treated this question at such unavoidable length because it is among the most important foundations of knowledge and the greatest questions concerning divine unity.

Completes the Ishāra ʿirfāniyya main text; printed p.467 opens a new numbered question. Does not establish the completeness of the whole Shawāriq.

WIT02 — The philosophical/Sufi contrast: under a condition versus without a condition

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Lāhījī, Shawāriq al-ilhām, ed. Asad ʿAlīzāda, I, p.469

Page-indexed electronic transcription checked against the displayed page; print image not collated

فيكون الفرق بين هذا المذهب، ومذهب الحكماء، انهم يخصون الواجبية بمرتبة واحدة؛ هي تلك الحقيقة بشرط أن لا يتعين بشيء من الماهيات. والصوفية يجعلون الواجبية لتلك الحقيقة؛ لا بشرط أن يتعين بشيء من الماهيات.

The difference between this position and that of the philosophers would be that the philosophers restrict necessity to one rank: that reality on condition that it not become determined by any of the quiddities. The Sufis, by contrast, assign necessity to that reality without making its non-determination by any quiddity a condition.

This proposal turns on bi-sharṭ lā versus lā bi-sharṭ; those logical qualifications cannot be collapsed into a physical division of one substance. | Bounded passage, not the whole work; do not infer an exhaustive manuscript collation.

WIT03 — Objection: a self-subsisting existence does not exclude dependent existences

ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī · Lāhījī, Shawāriq al-ilhām, ed. Asad ʿAlīzāda, I, p.473

Page-indexed electronic transcription checked against the displayed page; pp.470–472 not accessed

فمن أين يلزم أنه لا يكون وجود غير ذلك قائما بالماهيات الممكنة وأن يكون كل حقيقة وجودية قائمة بذاتها؟ وما ذكر من وجوب كون الوجود جزئيا حقيقيا، إنما هو في حقيقة وجودية قائمة بذاتها.

But whence does it follow that no existence other than this can subsist through contingent quiddities, and that every existential reality must subsist through itself? What was said about existence having to be a genuine particular applies only to an existential reality subsisting in itself.

This is a direct logical challenge to an inference from a unique necessary self-subsistent being to the denial of all dependent particular existences. | Bounded passage, not the whole work; do not infer an exhaustive manuscript collation.

Interim judgment: The texts do not produce one undifferentiated “mystical answer.” They map an argumentative space: radical monism, graded plural existence, unity under determinations, and theological affirmation of distinct dependent creatures. Q27 asks about logical support for the bridging inference; this question compares the actual doctrines and their critical reception.

Boundary: Historical anti-unity polemics and the full Dawwānī–Dashtakī manuscript exchange are still insufficiently represented; a final doctrinal verdict would exceed the available evidence.

Remaining: Lāhījī’s formerly missing electronic pp.470–472 are recovered and translated within the complete Ishāra main text (scan printed pp.462–466). Still required: independent edition/manuscript variants; direct verification of Jurjānī’s reported unity argument and Dawwānī’s adoption; the full original five-stage exchange and Ghiyāth’s response.

Q30 Unveiling, demonstration, presence, and imagination

How should claims of kashf, mushāhada and ʿilm ḥuḍūrī be related to rational proof and imaginative representation?

A demonstrative inference seeks shareable premises and a valid explanatory link; spiritual disclosure claims immediate access. It is misleading to say that one simply replaces reason by experience, or that a mystic’s claim can be judged by an entirely unrelated syllogism. The texts ask which kind of knowledge each path confers and whether it can rationally warrant metaphysical claims about the world.

Qūnawī claims another cognitive access

Qūnawī appeals to sound spiritual tasting and knowledge of the Real through the Real, arguing that the methods of the people of disclosure have an object and manner not exhausted by discursive proof.

A3 — Qūnawī: knowing the Real by the Real

al-Qūnawī · Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī · Conclusion of Question 1 (continuous passage)

Inherited extract: direct source/voice/collation still needs full audit

ونحن نقول: إنّ من مقتضى الذوق الصحيح الذي خطئ به أهل الحق منه سبحانه أنّ مبدأ معرفتهم معرفة الحق، لكن بالحق لا بقواهم وعقولهم. فإذا عرفوا الحق بالحق، عرفوا بعد ذلك نفوسهم بالحق من حيث ما عرفوه به، ثم عرفوا ما شاء الحق أن يطلعهم عليه دفعة أو بالتدريج. ولهذا يستحيل عندنا أن يعرف أحد حقيقة شيء، ما لم يعرف الحق. وقد ذكرنا قبل هذا على سبيل التلويح في التمهيد أنّ تعيّن الحق — سواء قيل بأنّ وجوده زائد على حقيقته أو أنّ وجوده عين حقيقته — في تعقّل كل عاقل لا يمكن أن يكون مطابقا لما هو الحق عليه في نفسه ولا لتعيّنه عند نفسه من حيث ما يمتاز عن سواه. فحينئذ سواء قول من يقول بأنّ وجود الحق عين حقيقته وقول من يقول بأنّ وجوده من لوازم حقيقته، لا يحصل من الأمرين تحقيق إذ لا يتمّ تقرير كل واحد من الأمرين.

We say that sound spiritual tasting [الذوق الصحيح], which the people of the Real have been granted by Him, entails that their knowing begins with knowledge of the Real—but through the Real, not through their own faculties and intellects. Once they know the Real through the Real, they know themselves through Him, in the respect in which they have known Him; thereafter they know whatever the Real wills to disclose to them, all at once or by stages. For this reason, in our view no one can know the reality of anything without knowing the Real. We indicated earlier, in the introduction, that the Real as determined in the conception of any intellectual knower—whether His existence is said to be additional to His reality or identical with it—cannot correspond to what the Real is in Himself, or to the determination He has for Himself insofar as He is distinguished from what is other than Him. Consequently, neither the claim that the Real’s existence is identical with His reality nor the claim that existence is a necessary concomitant of His reality yields a genuine realization [تحقيق]. Neither account can be established completely.

READING NOTE The epistemic claim is stronger than mere limits on natural theology: Qūnawī proposes the priority of divinely given knowledge of the Real. The online Arabic reads «خطئ به», which is awkward and likely a transcription error for «خُصّ به»; the translation follows the contextual sense “granted” pending collation against Schubert’s print edition. This uncertainty is not evidence of a variant manuscript reading. | Arabic source: https://www.ibnalarabi.com/qunawi/tusi.php?id=2

The precise contents claimed must be identified before an evidential assessment.

Ṭūsī’s reply is not a simple dismissal

Ṭūsī answers Qūnawī’s statement about unveiling while marking the limits of his treatment; in a separate reply he distinguishes his path from the path of kashf. These are different notes in the correspondence and must not be conflated.

A path’s difference from demonstration does not prove every claim made upon it.

The Sunni comparison of epistemic routes

Mullā ʿAlī al-Qārī reports Sufi training and purification, the theologians’ rational inference, and the claim that God is known through God. This is a taxonomy of methods, not a blanket endorsement or refutation of mystical metaphysics.

فمذهب الصوفية أن طريقها الرياضة والتخلية والتحلية وتصفية الطوية ... وذهب جمهور المتكلمين إلى أن طريقها إنما هو النظر والاستدلال ... وقال بعضهم يعرف الله بالله لا بغيره وهذا أشبه بمذهب الصوفية.

According to the Sufis, the path to [knowledge of God] is spiritual training, emptying and adorning [the soul], and purification of inward intention. ... The majority of theologians, by contrast, consider its route to be rational inquiry and inference. ... Others say that God is known through God, not through anything besides Him—an account closer to the Sufi path.

This is a polemical work and the classification of other schools is the polemicist’s; it should not be presented as a neutral or representative consensus. Keep it separate from the direct Tajrīd glosses.

Quṭb al-Dīn’s presence theory and Ṭihrānī’s classification of proof are developed separately in Q28 and Q11.

Interim judgment: The proper conclusion distinguishes the warrant of a claim to private insight, its public argumentative presentation, and the adequacy of its content under rational criticism. Neither all rational reasoning nor all spiritual knowledge is reducible to one logical procedure. The result does not pronounce that mystical witnessing proves numerical unity of existence.

Boundary: A critical edition still requires the complete relevant *Sharḥ al-Ishārāt* passages and context of the Qūnawī exchange before attributing a settled epistemological doctrine to Ṭūsī.

Remaining: Collate Ṭūsī’s separate Sharḥ al-Ishārāt (ninth and tenth namaṭs), direct Qūnawī–Ṭūsī correspondence, Sunni responses, and detailed Shīrāzī epistemology.
